text:
samir: FYI customer on enterprise plan is blocked after bumping our tagged v2 release. CI fails with a module path error and they also saw a spike of 401s in prod right after the commit landed.
henry: can you paste the repo go.mod and the exact go build error? sounds like a /v2 module path mismatch or a stray replace.
samir: customer provided a minimal repro (removed orgs):
```
# project go.mod
module github.com/acme/service

require (
    github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
)
```
build error they get: 
```
go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2
	but was required as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk
```
samir: they also pasted a snippet from our tagged tree showing the go.mod inside the tag still declares the old path (no /v2).
henry: that will make go tooling unhappy — when you tag a v2+ release the module path in the tagged source must include /v2. If it doesn't, `go get` fails like this.
emily: right — classic major-version-modpath mismatch. Two short-term customer options: pin to an earlier v1.x tag, or update their imports/go.mod to the /v2 module path.
qa-eli: repro steps I ran locally to confirm:
1) `GO111MODULE=on go env` (GOPROXY set to proxy.golang.org)
2) `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0` -> fails with same message
3) `git ls-remote --tags` shows v2.0.0 exists, so tag visibility is fine
qa-eli: inside our v2 tag I looked at go.mod: it still says `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` — that's the root cause.
samir: customer also saw 401s immediately after CI picked up the v2 tag. Any idea why they'd get auth errors too?
emily: possible that CI built a binary with different client code than dev (they mentioned a local replace/vendoring). A mismatch between what they tested and what CI pulled can change header formatting or auth logic and cause 401s. Also if tokens were rotated and the code variant doesn't include the new auth header, that explains it.
henry: do they use any `replace` directives or private mirrors? If so, dev vs CI behavior can differ.
samir: they said they had a `replace` to a private mirror for dev. CI doesn't include that replace, so CI ended up fetching the tagged release from proxy and hit the modpath mismatch.
emily: immediate remediation we suggested to the customer: 
- pin to the latest v1: `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v1.9.3` (unblocks them)
- or switch to v2 module path if they want v2: change `require` to `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 v2.0.0` and update imports to `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`
- short-term local workaround: add `replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk => ../go-sdk` while they test (not CI-safe)
henry: longer term, we need to fix our release process. Do we know intent at release time? A) intended to be proper v2 module path, or B) accidental v2 tags while still v1 module path?
samir: engineering confirms intent was A (module path bump to include /v2) but the tag was pushed before the go.mod change landed. Release script race.
emily: plan: create hotfix tag v2.0.1 where the go.mod inside the tag uses `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`. That should make `go get` happy. 
qa-eli: hotfix checklist: 
- update go.mod in the v2 branch to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`
- run `go mod tidy`, run unit tests and `go list ./...` in CI
- create annotated tag `v2.0.1` and push
- verify via `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.0.1` and check proxy visibility
henry: I'll own the hotfix. ETA ~2h. Also will add a CI gating check to fail tag creation if module path major mismatch detected.
dev-support-bot: Escalation created: #escalations-1773005678 assigned -> eng-release. Priority: P2. Ticket: RI-3421.
samir: customer pinned to v1.9.3 for now and is paused on deploy. They want an ETA to decide when to resume.
henry: v2.0.1 pushed and verified on proxy. I will post release notes and migration instructions in this thread.
emily: also adding a pre-tag check to our release script: compare tag major with `module` line and abort if mismatch.
samir: customer confirmed pinned v1 works, will test v2.0.1 later today. Closing loop once they confirm.
henry: raising a follow-up internal task to audit other modules for tag/modpath consistency.
summary: Customer CI/prod failures caused by go module major-version/tag mismatch: v2 tag published while go.mod still declared no /v2. Symptoms: `module declares its path` build error and runtime 401s caused by CI picking different client binary. Short-term workaround: pin to v1.9.3 or use replace. Fix: publish v2.0.1 with updated module path and add CI/tag checks.
